name: Line Enhancements
summary: Terminals, deliveries, costs, filter, toggles, names, demand, descents, fleet, timing, line button
description:
Improvements to lines. Each feature can be turned off in the mod's Settings (the gear next to the mod when choosing a game's mods). Settings also has a Logging switch, off by default, that writes the mod's messages to the game log (stdout.txt) for bug reports.

Assign Lines: an 'Assign Lines' button next to 'Configure' in the station window. It opens an Assign Lines window where you set each line's preferred and alternative terminals at this station. List view: drag a line by its grip onto another terminal to make it preferred, or drag the alternative handle on the right of the line to add the terminal as an alternative; alternatives are listed greyed below a separator, and the ✕ stops the line using that terminal. Grid view: left-click a line/terminal cell to make it preferred, right-click to add or remove it as an alternative. In both views, click a line's name to open its line window. In the statistics window's Stations tab, the Lines column gets an Assign Lines button at its right. Passenger lines can't use cargo-only terminals and vice versa. Colours show how a terminal suits a line: green = made for its cargo, yellow = made for other cargo (still usable, unloads slower), red = the line's trains can't reach it over the track.

Distribute Delivery: the stop window of the Line Manager gets a 'Distribute Delivery' button in its Load card. For each cargo the stop loads, it spreads the delivery over the following stops that accept that cargo, up to the next stop that loads it again: those stops get decreasing fill levels (for example 67 % and 33 % after a 100 % pickup), and the last one loads none of it, so the rest is delivered there. Hover the button to see the plan before applying it.

Send to Line remembers its filter: the Send to Line popover (vehicle window and Line Manager) opens with 'Show Only Visible Lines' set the way you last left it, for the rest of the session.

Toggle Passengers on All Stops: a button next to 'Set Line Color' in the Line Manager. If any stop of the selected lines loads passengers, it removes them from every stop; otherwise it adds them at every stop that allows passengers. With several lines selected it asks first.

Remove Cargo from All Stops: a cargo button after the passenger button. It is pressed while any stop of the selected lines loads cargo; click it to remove all cargo from every stop (fill levels are kept), e.g. to turn a line into a passenger-only line without editing each stop. With several lines selected it asks first.

Destination - Cargo names: Auto-Rename in the Line Manager gets a 'Destination - Cargo' suggestion, first in the list. A cargo line is named after the place it delivers to and the cargo it brings there, e.g. 'Colchester Steel Mill - Iron Ore' or 'Colchester Warehouse - Coal'. A line that takes cargo from warehouses out to a town's stops, the last leg of its delivery, becomes e.g. 'Culver City - Delivery Food'. A passenger line to an industry with workplaces becomes e.g. 'Colchester Workers - Steel Mill'. Other lines get the game's 'Town - Cargo' name.

Statistics - Cost Views: the statistics window's Lines tab gets three view buttons before the vehicle-type buttons. Lines: Utilization shows how much of its Rate the line used last year as a bar coloured green, yellow or red, beside the load right now; Balance becomes a bar on one scale for all lines, income to the right and costs to the left (running, servicing, track and signals, stations, depots; faded where shared with other lines); and a Net column takes off the line's share of upkeep that the game leaves out. Costs: every cost in its own sortable column, plus the upkeep only this line uses. Track: the fastest vehicle's top speed, the route by track or road type, and the km held back by curves, over-built (a cheaper track would do, with the upkeep it would save), under-built (with the time lost per round trip) and shared.

Line Cost Cards: the line window gets two cards that open like the game's own. Verdict: Profitable, Feeder or Unprofitable with the reason, and what the line earns, costs with all upkeep and enables (the lines carrying the output of an industry only this line supplies); open it for usage and what would help. Costs & Value: a waterfall from income to the net; open it for what the line enables, what removing it would change, and every cost.

District Colors in Line Manager: town buildings show their district colors (residential, commercial, industrial) in every view of the Line Manager, not only while you add or move a line's stops, so you can see where homes, shops and workplaces are while planning where a line should stop.

Station Catchment on Hover: select one line in the Line Manager (or edit its stops), then point at one of its stops or at any station on the map, also while adding a stop, and the town lots that station reaches turn orange. With several lines selected, or in Send to Line, the map is as usual.

Cargo Demand: select one or more cargo lines in the Line Manager (lines carrying the same cargo count together), or edit a line's stops, to see where the cargo is wanted. Over the town buildings that take the cargo, a yellow ! marks those the line's stops reach that hold none of it, and a red ? those in the line's towns that no stop reaches; pointing at a station (while adding a stop, or in the line's window) puts a blue pin on every building taking the cargo that it reaches and a red ? on every other one, so you see what that stop alone serves. The ! and ? also show while the line's own window is open. Under each town, every district shows a chip with the cargo and stored / capacity of its reached buildings (red empty, yellow part full, green full) and +n for buildings that take it but no stop reaches. The add stop, move stop and create line tooltips add what the station reaches, e.g. 'Vegetables: 7/24 in 9 buildings, 3 empty, 3 not yet on the line'.

Descent Zones: planes skip waypoints close to the airport they fly to. Once the flight still to go is about 10 times their height, they start descending and fly straight to the runway. Select one air line in the Line Manager and each airport it lands at shows a red circle where that happens (10 times its planes' cruise height), the straight path they then fly to the runway (for the earliest and the latest start of the descent) and a blue strip along the runway's approach line; waypoints all planes skip get a red dot, those only some planes skip an orange one. While you add or move a waypoint, its tooltip says whether planes landing at that leg's airport will skip it and how far it is from the runway line. Waypoints after takeoff are always flown.

Vehicle Load and Status: each vehicle in the Line Manager's vehicle list shows its load now (e.g. 30/30), its fullest departure of the last 20 with the stop's number in the stop list (e.g. 100% (4)), its average fill when leaving a stop (green from 67 %, yellow from 33 %, red below), and what it is doing and where: loading at stop 4 shows as 'Loading (4)', on the way there as 'En route → 4'; also circling an airport, waiting to take off, waiting at a signal or for a full terminal, in traffic, spacing out. A low average can hide one stop that needs the whole vehicle; the fullest departure shows it. The vehicle's name moves into the row's tooltip. The line window's Vehicles card shows the same as columns you can sort (largest first), with a locate pin and the vehicle's picture, which opens its window.

Stop Figures: a toggle at the end of the Line Manager's action bar (cargo and clock icon) turns the selected line's stop list into a Figures view, and back; the choice stays for every line until you change it. One row per stop and cargo: what waits there for this line (not the station's total for all lines), red over 3 vehicle loads and yellow over 1, the vehicle loads, the change since the last vehicle left (up / down arrow), the unhappy passengers and the arrivals a year. A stop that loads from industries' or warehouses' stocks shows their stock and what comes in a year; a stop that delivers cargo shows what the buildings and industries in reach hold of it and can take, e.g. 42/124, red when empty. Point at a stop's rows for a card beside the Line Manager with everything about it: where the passengers want to go, the station's total and more. While you add or move stops, the normal stop list shows.

Vehicles Needed: a card under the Line Manager's vehicle list, for one line. It measures how many passengers or how much cargo arrives at each stop a year and compares that with the seats the line offers (the game's Rate): '+3 to keep up', '+5 to clear the queues' (empty today's queue within 3 years), 'Enough vehicles' or how many fewer would still keep up. Open it with the arrow at its bottom right to try adding or removing vehicles of the line's model and see the interval, seats, each stop's queue (growing or shrinking, empty when), use and running costs before and after. Buying stays the Buy Vehicles button. Arrivals need a quarter of a game year of play before the card answers.

Line Timing: the Frequency alone can't say whether a line is slow, so the line window gets a Timing card after Vehicles: the normal loop (one vehicle round all stops on its best trips), the loop now (green, yellow or red against normal) and the frequency with its normal, then what slows the line, worst first, with what it costs in vehicles, e.g. 'Circling on the way to Hartha Airport: 1:31 a loop = 0.33 aircraft', longer stops, or a vehicle slow several loops in a row. Open it for each leg's normal against now, split into moving, the stop and each delay. The Line Manager's Frequency gets 'avg m:ss', the average time between departures from the first stop.

Manage Line Buttons: the Line Manager icon sits right of a line's name in a vehicle's window (its line), in a station window's Terminals card (each line) and in the statistics window's Lines tab. It opens the Line Manager on that line, as Manage Line in the line's window does, without opening the line's window first. The line window's Manage Line button shows the same Line Manager icon instead of the crossed arrows.

Selected Vehicle Count: the Line Manager's vehicle list shows how many of its vehicles are selected, as a number between the select-all box and the Reverse button (the tooltip adds how many are listed).

Recording: the game keeps no history per vehicle or stop, so the mod records departures, loads, arrivals and delays while the game runs and keeps them in the save (removing the mod leaves an unused table). Figures appear after the vehicles' next departures and grow more reliable over a game year.

A line's share of upkeep: each track or road piece on its route is split among the lines using it by vehicles passing, a station by stops, a depot by the vehicles it services. The figures can take a moment to appear after a window opens.

Thanks to square's Line Manager Plus for the idea of the vehicle details shown when hovering a vehicle's picture.

params.name: Assign Lines
params.tooltip: An Assign Lines button in the station window and the statistics Stations tab opens a window to set each line's preferred and alternative terminals.

params.name: Distribute Delivery
params.tooltip: A Distribute Delivery button in a stop's Load card shares a delivery out over the following stops that take the cargo, with decreasing fill levels.

params.name: Toggle Passengers on All Stops
params.tooltip: A button next to 'Set Line Color' in the Line Manager toggles passengers on every stop of the selected lines: it removes them while any stop loads passengers, otherwise adds them.

params.name: Remove Cargo from All Stops
params.tooltip: A cargo button after the passenger button in the Line Manager removes all cargo from every stop of the selected lines.

params.name: Destination - Cargo Names
params.tooltip: Auto-Rename in the Line Manager suggests names like 'Colchester Steel Mill - Iron Ore' or 'Colchester Workers - Steel Mill'.

params.name: District Colors in Line Manager
params.tooltip: Town buildings show their district colors (residential, commercial, industrial) in every view of the Line Manager, not only while you add or move stops.

params.name: Station Catchment on Hover
params.tooltip: With one line selected in the Line Manager, or while you edit its stops, pointing at a stop or station shows the town lots it reaches.

params.name: Cargo Demand
params.tooltip: With cargo lines selected in the Line Manager (their shared cargo), while you edit a line's stops, or in a line's window: over the buildings that take its cargo a yellow ! where its stops reach them and none is stored, a red ? where no stop reaches them, and while you point at a station blue pins on those it reaches and a red ? on all others, a stored / capacity chip per town district (+n buildings no stop reaches), and what a station reaches in the add stop tooltip.

params.name: Descent Zones
params.tooltip: With an air line selected in the Line Manager, each airport it lands at shows the circle where its planes start descending and skip waypoints, the straight path they then fly and the runway's approach line; skipped waypoints get a dot, and the waypoint tooltips warn about it.

params.name: Vehicle Load and Status
params.tooltip: Each vehicle in the Line Manager's vehicle list and the line window's Vehicles card (as sortable columns) shows its load now, its fullest departure with the stop, its average fill when leaving a stop and what it is doing (loading, circling, waiting at a signal, in traffic).

params.name: Stop Figures
params.tooltip: A toggle in the Line Manager's action bar turns the stop list into a table of figures per stop and cargo: what waits there for the line, vehicle loads, the change since the last vehicle left, unhappy passengers, arrivals a year; at delivery stops, what the buildings in reach hold. Point at a stop for a card with everything about it.

params.name: Vehicles Needed
params.tooltip: A card under the Line Manager's vehicle list says how many more vehicles keep up with the arrivals and how many also clear the queues; open it to try adding or removing vehicles.

params.name: Line Timing
params.tooltip: A Timing card in the line window compares the normal time round all stops with now, splits the delays by cause and place and names what slows the line; the Line Manager's Frequency gets its average.

params.name: Selected Vehicle Count
params.tooltip: The Line Manager's vehicle list shows how many vehicles are selected, beside its select-all box.

params.name: Statistics - Cost Views
params.tooltip: Lines, Costs and Track views in the statistics window's Lines tab: usage last year, a profit bar, the line's share of track, station and depot upkeep, and over- or under-built track.

params.name: Line Cost Cards
params.tooltip: Verdict and Costs & Value cards in the line window: what the line earns, costs with all upkeep and enables, and what would help.

params.name: Manage Line Buttons
params.tooltip: A Line Manager icon right of a line's name in the vehicle window, the station window's Terminals card and the statistics Lines tab opens the Line Manager on that line; the line window's Manage Line gets the same icon.

params.name: Send to Line Remembers Filter
params.tooltip: The Send to Line popover opens with 'Show Only Visible Lines' as you last left it.

params.name: Logging
params.tooltip: Writes the mod's messages to the game log (stdout.txt), for bug reports.
